predictions.explanation:
As of November 30, 2025, no company (including Google) has demonstrated a **large‑scale, fault‑tolerant quantum computer** capable of practically running Shor’s algorithm at scales that would *actually* break standard public‑key cryptosystems (e.g., 2048‑bit RSA, standard ECC curves) used on the internet.

Relevant current facts:

- Google’s major public milestones are still in the **noisy intermediate‑scale quantum (NISQ)** regime. After its 2019 “quantum supremacy” result with the 53‑qubit *Sycamore* processor, later work has focused on better qubits and error‑correction, not on a full‑scale, cryptography‑breaking device.
- Research papers and Google blog posts since then describe progress on **error-corrected logical qubits** and improved fidelities, but they do *not* claim any machine that can run Shor’s algorithm at cryptographically relevant sizes.
- Government and standards bodies are still operating under the assumption that **cryptography‑breaking quantum computers do *not* yet exist**, and are preparing via post‑quantum cryptography precisely because such machines are expected only in the future, on an uncertain timeline.

The prediction, however, explicitly allowed **3–7 years from around 2024** (i.e., roughly 2027–2031) for such a machine to exist *in principle* if Google continues on its trajectory. As of late 2025 we are only about **1–2 years** into that window. There is not yet evidence that Google has achieved this, but there is also not yet enough time elapsed to say definitively that it *won’t* by 2027–2031.

Because the prediction is about capabilities **by a future date that has not arrived yet**, and current evidence doesn’t falsify the possibility that Google might get there within that 3–7 year window, the correct status today is **“too early to tell.”**
predictions.grok_explanation: The prediction targets 2027–2031 for large-scale quantum computers running Shor's algorithm to break current encryption (e.g., RSA-2048). As of Dec 1, 2025 (1 year after podcast), no such computers exist. Google's Willow chip (105 qubits, Dec 2024) achieved quantum advantage via 'Quantum Echoes' algorithm (Oct 2025, [Google Blog](https://blog.google/technology/research/quantum-echoes-willow-verifiable-quantum-advantage/), [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/technology/google-says-it-has-developed-landmark-quantum-computing-algorithm-2025-10-22/)), but not Shor's or encryption-breaking; millions of qubits needed ([Quantum Insider, May 2025](https://thequantuminsider.com/2025/05/24/google-researcher-lowers-quantum-bar-to-crack-rsa-encryption/), [Cato Networks](https://www.catonetworks.com/blog/is-recent-quantum-hype-by-google-willows-chip-a-threat-to-rsa-algorithm/)). RSA unbroken ([PostQuantum, Apr 2025](https://postquantum.com/post-quantum/breaking-rsa-quantum-hype/)). Too early to evaluate.

predictions.explanation:
Keith’s prediction is explicitly about a **10‑year horizon** (“at least a decade out”) from 2024, i.e., roughly until 2034, so by November 2025 only ~1 year of that window has elapsed.

What we can check now is whether it has already been *falsified* by the emergence of clear commercial products or applications based on Google’s Willow‑type quantum computing:

- Google’s own announcement of the 105‑qubit Willow chip (Dec 9, 2024) frames it as a **research processor** demonstrating error correction and benchmark performance (Random Circuit Sampling), not as a commercial product, and emphasizes it as a step along a long‑term roadmap to *future* commercially relevant applications. ([blog.google](https://blog.google/technology/research/google-willow-quantum-chip/?utm_source=openai))
- Analyses in outlets like Forbes and think‑tank commentary likewise describe Willow as a **major research milestone** whose primary achievement is record‑breaking benchmarks and improved error correction; they note that practical or widespread commercial applications are still *several years away* and that current benchmarks (like RCS) have virtually no immediate practical utility. ([forbes.com](https://www.forbes.com/sites/moorinsights/2025/01/28/googles-105-qubit-willow-chip-achieves-major-quantum-milestones/?utm_source=openai))
- Coverage in The Verge and other sources underscores that Willow is *not yet* at the scale needed for real‑world cryptanalytic or other mission‑critical applications, with timelines for such impact still estimated at least many years out. ([theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/2024/12/12/24319879/google-willow-cant-break-rsa-cryptography?utm_source=openai))
- Google continues to report **research achievements** with Willow—e.g., a 2025 “verifiable quantum advantage” experiment—again framed as a scientific milestone rather than a commercial product offering to customers. ([blog.google](https://blog.google/technology/research/quantum-hardware-verifiable-advantage/?utm_source=openai))

As of Nov 30, 2025, there is **no evidence** that Willow or closely related Google superconducting, error‑corrected processors have been turned into generally available, revenue‑driving commercial products or deployed applications with clear business value; they remain in the realm of advanced research and experimental cloud access.

However, because the claim is that **no true commercial products or applications will emerge for about 10 years**, and we are nowhere near 2034 yet, we can’t say whether the 10‑year timescale will ultimately prove right or wrong. So the prediction is **not yet falsified**, but also **not yet confirmed**.

Therefore the correct status as of now is: it’s **too early to tell** — *inconclusive*.

predictions.explanation: Trump’s second administration implemented aggressive trade measures in 2025 that directly hit Shein’s U.S. business model. In April–May 2025, Trump imposed minimum tariffs of about 145% on Chinese goods and moved to end the de minimis exemption that had allowed most Shein shipments under $800 to enter the U.S. duty‑free, a provision specifically cited as crucial to the growth of Shein and Temu. ([washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2025/04/15/china-tariffs-shein-temu-de-minimis/?utm_source=openai)) Facing these policy changes, Shein warned U.S. customers of price hikes, cut advertising, and experienced a sharp decline in U.S. sales, according to market and retail reporting. ([washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2025/11/28/temu-shein-black-friday-sales/?utm_source=openai)) Reuters and other outlets reported that Shein began considering a restructuring of its U.S. operations and exploring relocation of production for U.S.-bound goods in response to the new tariff risks, which were also clouding its planned London IPO. ([reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/shein-weighs-us-restructuring-tariff-risks-cloud-london-ipo-ft-reports-2025-04-30/?utm_source=openai)) Later in 2025, Trump signed an order globally suspending the de minimis exemption, further tightening the trade environment for firms like Shein. ([forbes.com](https://www.forbes.com/sites/zacharyfolk/2025/07/30/trump-suspends-de-minimis-tariff-exemption-for-goods-under-800/?utm_source=openai)) Although Shein remains active in the U.S. and has started to recover some demand, contemporaneous coverage describes the tariffs and shipping‑rule changes as having caused significant operational and growth challenges for Shein and similar platforms. ([washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2025/11/28/temu-shein-black-friday-sales/?utm_source=openai)) These developments align closely with the prediction that Shein would face “real problems” in the new Trump administration via regulatory, tariff, or trade actions that materially impede its U.S. operations and growth.

predictions.explanation:
Evidence shows that after Trump took office again in January 2025, the U.S. did in fact implement substantial new tariff measures specifically targeting imports from China, beyond the tariff regime in place as of December 2024 under Biden.

By late 2024, Chinese imports were already subject to Section 301 tariffs, and the Biden administration had *finalized* and begun implementing additional increases on selected Chinese products—such as EVs, solar cells, semiconductors, batteries, and certain metals—raising many of these duties to 25–100% on a limited, sectoral basis.([ustr.gov](https://ustr.gov/about-us/policy-offices/press-office/press-releases/2024/may/us-trade-representative-katherine-tai-take-further-action-china-tariffs-after-releasing-statutory?utm_source=openai)) These were in place or scheduled prior to Trump’s January 2025 inauguration and form the December 2024 baseline.

In Trump’s second term, however, the White House introduced **broad, additional tariffs across essentially all imports from China**, clearly exceeding that baseline:

* On **February 1, 2025**, Trump signed executive orders imposing a new 10% tariff on *all* Chinese imports **on top of existing China duties**, with effect from February 4, 2025.([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_United_States_trade_war_with_Canada_and_Mexico?utm_source=openai))  
* On **March 3, 2025**, he raised this China-wide surcharge from 10% to 20%, again in addition to the existing Section 301 rates.([zh.wikipedia.org](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E4%B8%AD%E7%BE%8E%E8%B4%B8%E6%98%93%E6%88%98?utm_source=openai))  
* On **April 2, 2025**, Trump announced further sweeping tariffs, including an **additional 34% on Chinese goods**. Reporting and official/analytical sources describe this package as lifting total U.S. tariffs on Chinese products to around **54%**, and closing the de minimis loophole for low-value Chinese shipments (e.g., Shein, Temu) so they no longer enter duty-free.([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/apr/03/china-condemns-unilateral-bullying-as-it-calls-on-us-to-drop-tariffs?utm_source=openai))  

These measures were widely characterized as the most significant U.S. protectionist action since the 1930s, with China singled out for especially high combined rates.([pt.wikipedia.org](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarifas_do_Dia_da_Liberta%C3%A7%C3%A3o?utm_source=openai)) Although a federal court later struck down much of the broad “Liberation Day” tariff program, it did so **after** these China-focused surcharges had been imposed, and some product-specific measures remained in effect.([washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2025/05/28/trump-tariffs-trade-court-ruling/?utm_source=openai))

Given that (1) a Trump administration did begin in January 2025, and (2) that administration **implemented large, new, China-targeted tariffs on top of the December 2024 regime**, Keith Rabois’s prediction that “you’re going to see real tariffs, especially against China” is **right** in substance.

predictions.explanation:
As of November 30, 2025, it is too early to judge Chamath’s 2–5 year prediction.

Key facts:
- Google’s Willow processor, announced in December 2024, has 105 *physical* superconducting qubits and demonstrates a few *logical* qubits with below‑threshold error correction, not thousands of logical qubits.([blog.google](https://blog.google/technology/research/google-willow-quantum-chip/?utm_source=openai))
- Google itself and outside analysts emphasize that Willow is **far** from a “cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer”: estimates for breaking RSA‑2048 still sit around **millions of physical qubits** (roughly 4 million), with timelines typically **a decade or more away**, not 1–2 years.([theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/2024/12/12/24319879/google-willow-cant-break-rsa-cryptography?utm_source=openai))
- Current overviews of quantum progress in 2025 describe systems in the ~10²–10³ qubit range and consistently state that we are still far from the fault‑tolerant, large‑scale machines needed to break RSA‑2048 or Bitcoin’s SHA‑256/ECDSA security; those capabilities are generally projected into the 2030s or later.([forbes.com](https://www.forbes.com/sites/leeorshimron/2025/06/30/quantum-threat-bitcoins-fight-to-secure-our-digital-future/?utm_source=openai))
- Policy and cybersecurity guidance (e.g., UK NCSC) likewise targets around **2035** as the planning horizon for serious quantum decryption threats, reinforcing that no such capability exists yet.([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/mar/20/uk-cybersecurity-agency-quantum-hackers?utm_source=openai))
- There is no public evidence by late 2025 that RSA‑2048 has been broken by a quantum computer or that Bitcoin’s core cryptography has been compromised; instead, industry and governments are still treating this as a **future** risk and rolling out post‑quantum standards (e.g., NIST PQC).([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NIST_Post-Quantum_Cryptography_Standardization?utm_source=openai))

Because Chamath’s stated window is **2–5 years from 2024** (roughly 2026–2029), and only about one year has elapsed, we cannot yet say definitively whether quantum hardware will fail or succeed in reaching the ~4,000–8,000 logical‑qubit scale in that period. The current trajectory makes the prediction look very optimistic, but the deadline has not passed, so the correct classification for now is **"inconclusive (too early)"**.

predictions.grok_explanation: As of December 2025, no quantum computer has achieved 4,000 logical qubits. Highest records include Quantinuum's 50 entangled logical qubits (Dec 2024) and Helios with 48 logical qubits from 98 physical qubits (Nov 2025); Microsoft/Atom with 24 logical qubits (Nov 2024). Google's Willow (105 physical qubits, Dec 2024) demonstrates error-corrected logical qubits like a 7x7 surface code (one logical qubit), equated by the predictor to ~1 stable logical qubit, far below thresholds for breaking RSA-2048 (~4,000 logical) or SHA-256 (~8,000). Articles confirm Willow cannot threaten cryptography, needing millions of qubits. Prediction timeframe: 2-5 years from Dec 2024 (2026-2029); only ~11 months passed. Sources: [Google Willow blog](https://blog.google/technology/research/google-willow-quantum-chip/), [Quantinuum Helios](https://www.quantinuum.com/blog/introducing-helios...), [HPCwire on Willow](https://www.hpcwire.com/2025/10/22/google-claims-quantum-advantage-with-willow-chip/), [Science.org](https://www.science.org/content/article/new-more-stable-qubits...), CCN Bitcoin risk article.
